## Summary

`npm run build` in `packages/herdr` exits 2 with 84 `TS6059` errors (`File ... is not under 'rootDir' '/home/.../packages/herdr/src'`).

## Root cause

`packages/herdr/tsconfig.json` sets `rootDir: ./src` and includes `src/**/*.ts`, which includes the `.test.ts` files. Several herdr test files (e.g. `src/implement-tier-blocked-exclusion.test.ts`, worklist tests) import shared CLI test helpers from the repo root (`../../tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`, `../../src/*`). Those files are pulled into the compilation graph but lie outside `rootDir`, producing TS6059 for every import. tsc still emits the in-root files to `dist/`, but the `cp src/shortcuts.json dist/shortcuts.json` step of the build script never runs (tsc exits non-zero), leaving `dist/shortcuts.json` stale.

## Expected behaviour

- `cd packages/herdr && npm run build` exits 0 and copies `src/shortcuts.json` → `dist/shortcuts.json`.

## Implementation notes

- Exclude test files from the herdr build: add `"exclude": ["**/*.test.ts"]` to `packages/herdr/tsconfig.json` (the test files are compiled/run by vitest, not needed in dist). Verify `npm run build` exits 0 and `dist/` contains no `.test.js` files.
- Check whether `packages/shared/tsconfig.json` has the same pattern (it builds cleanly today — likely no test files there).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cd packages/herdr && npm run build` exits 0.
- [ ] `dist/shortcuts.json` is copied on every build.
- [ ] `npx vitest run packages/herdr` still passes (tests unaffected by the exclude).

Discovered from: WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4

# Intake Brief: Herdr hydrator — rescue in_progress work items with no active pane

## Headline

Add a hydration task to the herdr worklist plugin that, every 30 seconds, fetches all `in_progress` work items, matches each against the work-item IDs embedded in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace (via the pane-title work WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), and demotes any item with no matching pane out of `in_progress` to `completed` (stage `in_review`), `blocked` (dependency-blocked), or `open` (otherwise). The check also runs immediately when the tab regains focus.

## Problem statement

Work items are sometimes left stuck in `status=in_progress` even though no agent pane is actually working on them (e.g. the agent pane was closed, the session died, or the item was claimed and abandoned). There is currently no automatic mechanism to detect this, so stale in-progress items linger at the top of work queues and are never re-selected.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want a self-healing work queue where an item only stays `in_progress` while an active agent pane is genuinely attached to it.
  - As a producer, I want items whose agent pane has died to be demoted automatically so they re-enter the selection pool instead of rotting in `in_progress`.
- **Herdr worklist users** — benefit from a queue that reflects reality without manual cleanup.
  - As a user, I want the worklist to keep `in_progress` items only when a matching pane exists, so the list stays honest.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every 30 seconds the hydrator fetches all `in_progress` work items (`wl list --status in_progress`).
2. For each item, the hydrator attempts to match an **active pane**: a pane, in **any tab of the current workspace**, whose pane title contains the work item's ID (`WL-…`) and that is still running (present in `herdr pane list`). Matching relies on the pane-title format introduced by the blocking work item (e.g. `Manually triggered implement <title> - WL-<id>`).
3. Any `in_progress` item with **no matching active pane** is demoted:
   - stage `in_review` → `status=completed`
   - item has an active outbound dependency blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`) → `status=blocked`
   - otherwise → `status=open`
   Transitions respect the project's status/stage compatibility rules (e.g. `blocked` only allows stages `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`, so a stage `in_progress` item demoted to `blocked` must also have its stage demoted).
4. When the worklist tab regains focus, the hydration check runs **immediately** (not waiting for the next 30s tick), reusing the existing visibility resume-poll mechanism.
5. The hydrator is **safe**: no transition is made for an item whose matching pane is found; the task is single-flight; failures (CLI missing, unparseable output) are logged and never crash the plugin; no `wl` spawns happen while the worklist pane is hidden.
6. Unit tests cover: pane-title ID extraction, active-pane matching across tabs, each demotion decision (in_review→completed, dependency-blocked→blocked, else→open), stage/status compatibility handling, focus-resume immediate run, and fail-open error paths.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked on WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** ("Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned") — the hydrator matches panes by the work-item ID embedded in pane titles; it must not be implemented before that title format lands. (The in-progress duplicate WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D carries the same work; block on the intake-complete one.)
- The 30s loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker) — acceptable per the operator; the focus-resume immediate check is required.
- "Active pane" = any running pane whose title contains the work-item ID, across **all tabs** in the current workspace; focus/zoom state does not matter (matching is by title presence + pane existence, not focus).
- Reuse the existing `TaskScheduler` (packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts) and the visibility `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery in `worklist.ts`; do not add a second interval loop.
- Fail-open at every boundary: never crash the plugin, never demote on ambiguous evidence (missing pane list, unparseable output → treat as "no match" only when the CLI output is actually trustworthy).
- No schema changes; pure status/stage updates via the `wl` CLI.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the worklist TUI registers a single `TaskScheduler` with tasks: `refresh` (auto-refresh), `sync`, `resume-poll` (hidden→visible immediate refresh), and `downtime` (downtime-worker tick, 30s default). The hydrator would be a sibling task.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — `TaskScheduler` with 1s base tick, per-task `intervalMs`, `singleFlight`, and `runTimeoutMs` watchdog; a rejecting task never takes down the loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — `isPaneVisible()` + `PollGate` (TTL memoizer); tab focus via `herdr tab get <id>` is the visibility signal; resume-poll uses it to detect hidden→visible.
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — existing work-item ↔ pane association file (`.worklog/agent-panes.json`) and `herdr agent list` parsing; a possible secondary signal but the hydrator matches by pane-title per the operator's decision.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `runWl(...)`, `extractJson`, `extractItems` helpers for wl CLI JSON.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/toggle.sh` — precedent for `herdr pane list` JSON parsing (panes with `label`/`pane_id` across the workspace).
- `src/commands/dep.ts` — `wl dep list <id>` returns `outbound` edges with target `id`/`status`/`priority`; `packages/shared/src/database.ts:isDependencyActive` defines an active blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`).
- `src/config.ts` — status/stage compatibility: `in-progress` allows `intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`; `blocked` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`; `completed` allows `in_review`/`done`; `open` allows `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`.

## Desired change

1. Add a hydrator module (e.g. `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`):
   - `extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes)` — parse `WL-[0-9A-Z]+` from pane titles.
   - `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes)` — item ID present in any running pane title across all tabs.
   - `decideDemotion(item)` — pure decision: `in_review` → `completed`; dependency-blocked → `blocked`; else → `open` (with stage/status compatibility handling).
   - `runHydrationOnce(deps)` — fetch `wl list --status in_progress`, fetch `herdr pane list`, match, apply demotions via `wl update`.
2. Register the hydrator in `worklist.ts` as a scheduler task (`id: 'hydrate'`, `intervalMs: 30_000`, `singleFlight: true`, `runTimeoutMs` set) that is visibility-gated (skip while hidden, zero wl spawns when hidden).
3. Hook the hidden→visible transition: when the resume-poll detects visibility, run the hydration check immediately in addition to the existing refresh.
4. Add unit tests (see AC6) mirroring the existing downtime-worker test harness (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, injectable exec seam from `fetcher.ts`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — new module: ID extraction, pane matching, demotion decision, orchestration (the bulk of the work).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — register the `hydrate` scheduler task; trigger immediate check on focus-resume.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — reused as-is (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — reused `runWl`/`extractJson`/`extractItems` helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — reused `PollGate`/resume-poll machinery (no changes expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — new test suite (AC6).
- `src/config.ts` — reference only: status/stage compatibility rules that constrain demotion.
- `src/commands/dep.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — reference only: dependency-blocked semantics (`isDependencyActive`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y** — "Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned" (open, intake_complete) — **BLOCKING**: introduces the pane-title format containing the work-item ID that the hydrator matches on. In-progress duplicate: **WL-0MSJ4E5BM000LE3D** (same title).
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** — "Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon" (in_review) — pane↔work-item association machinery; `agent-panes.json` is a candidate secondary signal.
- **WL-0MS9NPHQU005Y3VE** — "Herdr plugin should set work-item status to in_progress when instigating actions" (completed) — the counter-direction: sets `in_progress` on dispatch; the hydrator demotes when no pane remains.
- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime" (completed) — downtime worker: the 30s scheduler-task precedent the hydrator mirrors.
- **WL-0MSJNJPRM009RM35** — "Gate worklist auto-refresh on tab focus so a visible pane in a multi-pane tab keeps refreshing" (in_progress) — visibility-gating precedent reused by the hydrator.
- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — "Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible" (completed) — related zero-spawn-when-hidden concern.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** pane titles will contain the work-item ID once WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y lands — the hydrator is blocked on that and must not guess other signals.
- **Risk:** demoting an item the operator considers genuinely in-progress (pane title missing/renamed by hand, pane in a different workspace). Mitigation: matching is by title + pane existence across all tabs; the 30s cadence + focus-resume means demotions are re-visible quickly; keep the demotion decision pure and well-tested.
- **Risk:** status/stage compatibility rejects a demotion (e.g. `blocked` with stage `in_progress`). Mitigation: `decideDemotion` returns a compatible (status, stage) pair; transitions that fail validation are logged, not retried blindly.
- **Risk:** `herdr pane list` output shape differs (tabs vs panes). Mitigation: fail-open parsing like toggle.sh/agent-tracker; treat unparseable output as "no demotion this cycle".
- **Risk:** scope creep (agent-panes.json matching, notifications, configurable intervals). Mitigation: record as linked work items; this intake covers pane-title matching only.
- **Scope-creep guard:** secondary signals (agent-panes.json, `herdr agent list` states) are explicitly out of scope for the initial implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When no active pane matches an in_progress item, HOW should the hydrator choose between completed / blocked / open? (a) Signal-based: stage in_review → completed; blocked-by dependencies → blocked; otherwise → open; (b) always open; (c) operator picks per item; (d) other" — Answer (user): **a** — signal-based. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "The herdr plugin's 30s scheduler loop runs inside the worklist pane process (like the downtime worker). That means the hydrator only runs while a worklist pane is open. Acceptable, or should it run standalone?" — Answer (user): **acceptable**, ensure the check runs immediately when the tab gets focus. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Does 'active pane' mean any pane whose title contains the work-item ID and is still running (regardless of focus/zoom), across all tabs in the current workspace?" — Answer (user): **yes**. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1** – wl next should return parent items instead of surfacing children individually (completed)
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** – Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item and show their status icon (completed)
- **WL-0MSC0O8HN000EBFH** – Herdr plugin: free-form prompt shortcut opens new pi pane (option B) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-Herdr-hydrator-rescue-in-progress-work-items-with-no-active-pane-WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI.md` — matched: 000, 0ms9nphqu005y3ve, 0msb1n0hb0007n6n, 0msbqujqx005rat9, 0msf49fmw009m06k (+409 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSOKOI4J0046GE5-remove-stray-compiled-artifacts-committe/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 000, 0msb1n0hb0007n6n, 0msf49fmw009m06k, 0msjnjprm009rm35, 30s (+272 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 000, 0msb1n0hb0007n6n, 0msf49fmw009m06k, 0msjnjprm009rm35, 30s (+272 more)

data.description: Discovered-from: WL-0MSGI7UIH008USVB. skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py run_suite() (line ~318) and run_summary() (line ~526) call node_suite_commands() with NO project_root, so commands are built from the framework REPO_ROOT (~/.pi/agent → SorraAgents) while executing with cwd=detected project root (ContextHub). Result: for non-framework repos with npm 'test' script (vitest), the canonical node suite is emitted as framework-relative 'node --test tests/<dir>/**/*.mjs' globs that match nothing in the target repo — vacuous green, no real tests run. The audit skill's _effective_suite_commands() correctly calls full_suite_commands(project_root), so it queries 'npm --silent test -- tests/cli' etc. — causing a cache MISS mismatch unless the cache is populated with the project-root-aware commands directly. Fix: pass project_root through to node_suite_commands() in run_suite()/run_summary().
data.title: test skill: node_suite_commands() ignores detected project root (vacuous node suite for non-framework repos)

## Problem statement

During the 2026-08-20 system hang, \"Under memory pressure, flushing caches\" appeared 10+ times in the journal between 13:27 and 13:40 with no alert and no early warning. The system ran for 21 days with accumulating memory pressure and no monitoring to catch it before it became unusable.

## Goal

Install lightweight memory-pressure monitoring so a repeat of the 2026-08-20 memory exhaustion is detected and alerted on well before the system becomes unresponsive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A monitoring mechanism is installed (e.g. cron/systemd timer script checking /proc/meminfo MemAvailable, or earlyoom/PSI-based monitoring via /proc/pressure/memory)
- [ ] An alert fires when MemAvailable drops below a threshold (e.g. 2 GB) - alert method documented (logger/journald entry, desktop notification, or both)
- [ ] Historical trend is captured so memory exhaustion can be diagnosed after the fact (e.g. collectd/sysstat already captures sar data - verify and document retention)
- [ ] The alert mechanism is tested end-to-end once (verified alert emission)
- [ ] Setup and thresholds documented in a comment on this work item or docs

## Suggested approach

```bash
# /etc/cron.d/memwatch (example)
* * * * * root [ $(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo) -lt 2048 ] && logger -p user.warning "LOW MEMORY: $(awk '/MemAvailable/ {printf \"%.0fMB
\", $2/1024}' /proc/meminfo)"
```

Consider also monitoring /proc/pressure/memory (PSI) for sustained pressure events, which is what journald's \"Under memory pressure\" messages derive from.

## Key files

- /proc/meminfo, /proc/pressure/memory, /var/log/sysstat (sar data if installed)
- Discovered from: RCA of system hang 2026-08-20 (session analysis; no parent work item)

# Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork`) and the Herdr extension selection list (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` → `worklist.ts`) disagree on "most important item" because the dispatcher maintains its own tier ordering (`wl next --stage …` per tier + `wl list` audit query) instead of reusing the Herdr list. The project needs the dispatcher to consume the Herdr list head so the two selectors agree by construction. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`" scope per producer determination WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 (2026-09-02).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs a single trustworthy queue; the item dispatched during downtime was visible at the top of `prefix+l` and reflects declared prioritization intent.
- **Herdr user browsing `prefix+l`** — expects downtime work to track exactly what the visible list shows, so automated work does not appear arbitrary.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl next** — needs a single ranking contract; ranking logic lives only in the fetcher/smart-selection/grouping/database pipeline.

Example user stories:
- As a producer, I want the downtime dispatcher to pick the first item shown in the Herdr list, so automated work follows the priority I already see.
- As a herdr user, when downtime dispatches `/skill:implement WL-XYZ`, I want WL-XYZ to have been at the head of the Herdr list, so I understand why it was chosen.
- As a maintainer, I want the ranking contract documented as "dispatcher == Herdr list head" so future safety gates are evaluated as filters, not a competing ranking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dispatcher consumes Herdr list head** — `dispatchDowntimeWork` (and any coordination-leader path) derives its candidate from the Herdr selection list head rather than a separate tier ordering / stage-scoped `wl next` / `wl list` audit query. No second ranking implementation remains on the dispatch path.
2. **No duplicate ranking; gates are filters** — tier ordering / `wl next --stage` per-tier calls / audit `wl list` ranking are no longer used to pick "most important". Any safety gates that must remain (code-freeze skip, dispatched-marker exclusion, active-audit single-flight, per-process single-flight / CAS claim) act as sequential filters on the Herdr-ordered candidates. If no Herdr-ordered candidate passes the filters, the dispatcher reports "no candidate" rather than falling back to a separate ranking.
3. **Herdr list remains sole ranking path** — `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` / `regroupWorkItems` stay the sole ranking path (mandatory-always for critical + `completed`/`in_review`, `browseItemCount` windowing of "other" items, grouping logic, `reSort`/`computeScore` as used by the fetcher). No `wl next`/`database.ts` scoring change is required to fix the divergence; if `fetchNextItems` delegates to `wl next` internally that internal detail is acceptable — the observable contract is "dispatcher == Herdr list head".
4. **Contract documented** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` (and `src/commands/next.ts` help if it references dispatcher selection) state explicitly: dispatcher selects the first dispatchable item from the Herdr selection list; any remaining safety override (e.g. code-freeze) is documented as a skip/filter on that sequence, not a ranking.
5. **No regression; observable agreement proven** — existing `wl next` / herdr fetcher/grouping / downtime-worker fixtures pass; a reproducible sampling script shows `wl next -n` / Herdr list / downtime pick agree (downtime picks the list head after filtering) on a fixture. Dispatched-marker / code-freeze / single-flight gating still respected as filters on the Herdr sequence.

## Constraints

- Zero npm deps for herdr; `smart-selection.ts`/`grouping.ts` duplicated per TUI stays in sync with `src/commands/*` if touched.
- `browseItemCount` clamping (1–50) and root-only / `done`-exclusion rules respected.
- Do not fork a second ranking; reuse the Herdr list pipeline.
- Investigation only touched the prior item (WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q); this item carries the implementation.
- Backwards compat: existing dispatched-marker / code-freeze gating semantics preserved as filters.

## Existing state

- **Herdr list:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` runs `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` unless `--no-re-sort`), merges mandatory subsets via `fetchMandatorySubsets` (`wl list --priority critical --root-only` and `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`), applies `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` (root-only, `stage != done`, mandatory always shown, `browseItemCount` limits only "other" items), and regroups with `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` / `assignItemGroups` (Critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review). Rendered via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **Downtime dispatcher:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` — tier order audit → implement (`wl next --stage plan_complete` with risk/effort caps) → plan (`wl next --stage intake_complete`) → fallback idea (`wl next --stage idea`); audit tier uses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` with 7-day recency / dispatched-marker / active-audit / code-freeze gates; pre-dispatch CAS claim, per-process single-flight, scheduled-prompts tier, round-robin cursor, cooldowns.
- **Shared scoring:** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (`computeScore`/`reSort`/`filterCandidates`/`findNextWorkItemFromItems`) and `src/commands/next.ts` auto `reSort` — shared by `wl next` but not required to change for this contract; the observable contract is Herdr list head.
- All divergence gaps mapped in WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q (cap 32 / mandatory merge / stage-scoped calls / audit `wl list` source / tier order / risk-effort gates / code-freeze tri-state, etc.) — eliminated by consuming the Herdr order directly.

## Desired change

Replace the dispatcher's independent tier ordering with consumption of the Herdr selection list head:

- Refactor `downtime-worker.ts` to invoke (or share code with) the Herdr fetcher/selection pipeline to obtain the ordered candidate sequence, then apply only the necessary safety filters (code-freeze, dispatched-marker, single-flight/active-audit) sequentially on that sequence.
- Remove or dead-code the tier-ordering / per-stage `wl next` / audit `wl list` ranking path from the dispatch decision (or leave only as unused fallback behind a feature flag with a clear deprecation note).
- Document the contract ("dispatcher == Herdr list head; filters, not ranking") in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Herdr selection pipeline reused by dispatcher
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — mandatory-always + browseItemCount logic
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — regroupWorkItems / assignItemGroups ordering
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — rendering consuming grouped selection
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatchDowntimeWork to be refactored to consume list head (+ fixtures)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — computeScore/reSort/filterCandidates as used by fetcher (not dispatcher ranking)
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/grouping.ts` — wl next entry point as used by fetcher
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher contract doc
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr list contract doc

## Related work

- Investigation: WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q — downtime dispatcher vs herdr selection list divergence (producer determination revised 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, superseding WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS) → follow-up direction is this item.
- WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX — counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect (symptom of cap/mandatory interaction; not blocking but shares fetcher context)
- WL-0MS8XL3EW006Y04G / WL-0MSKCRX730052iiw / WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G / WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR — Herdr smart selection / in_review / root-only rules shaping mandatory set
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 / WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG — implement tier + risk/effort filters wired into wl next / dispatcher (removed or converted to filters in this work)
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY / WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN / WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — dispatched-marker exclusion, conditional claim, dispatch logging (preserved as filters)
- WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6 — priority-first with round-robin tie-break (cursor handling to reconcile with Herdr order)
- RCA docs: `downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`, `downtime-disable-incident-rca-2026-08-22.md` — prior tier/re-dispatch incidents

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "selection list" means herdr `prefix+l` Work Items list (`fetchNextItems` path); "downtime dispatcher" means `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier loop in `downtime-worker.ts` (including coordination leader path if any).
- Assumption: producer wants a single notion of "most important" — confirmed 2026-09-02 (Herdr list canonical; dispatcher consumes head).
- Risk: code-freeze / audit safety behavior at head — if the list head must be skipped, the skip order must be explicit and remain a filter on the Herdr sequence; document clearly.
- Risk: `in_review` mandatory-always items in the list — dispatcher taking the head must still respect `completed`/`in_review` dispatchability; filter vs ranking distinction must be explicit to avoid re-dispatching audits.
- Risk: spare-capacity / idle-budget / round-robin cursor logic must be reconciled as filters or removed; otherwise a second ordering re-emerges.
- Scope-creep risk: unifying ranking touches herdr selection and downtime-worker — keep scope to dispatcher-consumes-head; do not rework scoring or grouping unless required for the contract. Extra opportunities → new work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When you say 'most important,' do you mean the Herdr list order or the dispatcher tier order?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, rescoping WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2; supersedes WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS): **Herdr extension selection list order is authoritative** (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`). Dispatcher selects the first item in that list — no second ranking. Source: producer comment WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.
- Q2: "Should the two selectors be unified to one shared ranking, or should the dispatcher intentionally differ (e.g. audit-first)?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **Unified on the Herdr list** — single source of truth; dispatcher consumes the list head. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`". Source: same producer determination.

# Child 1: Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`) runs `UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed. Re-sort runs automatically on `wl next` (unless `--no-re-sort`), on create/update, so routine queue reads rewrite `updatedAt` on dozens of items at once (observed: 13 items at `2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z`, 88 items at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`).

The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: audit counts only if `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats those items as edited-after-audit. Concrete victim: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V audited "Ready to close: Yes" 2026-09-03 now carries `updatedAt` 2026-09-11, so its passing audit reads stale and the item lingers in the open queue. Recency-weighted scoring (`database.ts:2215-2216`) is also polluted.

## Users

- **Producer/operator:** a "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical re-sorts.
- **Heartbeat/audit pipeline:** must not re-audit items whose only change is sortIndex.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batchUpdateSortIndices` (and the `database.ts:755-767` single-item re-sort path) no longer bump `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`. Semantic edits elsewhere still bump `updatedAt` as today.
- [ ] Regression test: audit an item "Ready to close: Yes", run `reSort`, assert the audit is still fresh (`auditedAt >= updatedAt` holds / freshness check passes) and `updatedAt` is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression test: a genuine semantic edit after audit still invalidates freshness (existing WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 behavior preserved).
- [ ] Existing re-sort / sync / audit tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Surgical change in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts` only. No schema migration.
- Check sibling: WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt) — fix here must not conflict; note interaction in a comment.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769` — `batchUpdateSortIndices`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:755-793` — re-sort paths; `:644` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh`; `:2215` — recency scoring
- `src/commands/re-sort.ts`

## Related work

- WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 (freshness rule — preserve for semantic edits)
- WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (sibling timestamp symptom)
- WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF, WL-0MOYD0UAC003YJA3, WL-0MNX9XIQD005PUVW (auto re-sort features)

# Intake Brief — Smart Audit Re-instatement

**Headline:** When the audit freshness check (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) flags an audit as stale, the system should automatically review the changes made since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or flag the item for re-audit — rather than treating all post-audit changes as requiring a full re-run.

## Problem statement

Audits are invalidated whenever a work item's `updatedAt` changes after the audit time (`isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`). However, many changes do not affect the code or implementation that was audited (e.g., changing a comment, updating assignee). The audit skill should automatically inspect the changes since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or require a new one.

**Producer clarification:** The system should inspect anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it — description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl next` / Pi TUI:** Audited items should not be unnecessarily re-audited when changes are irrelevant to the implementation.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher:** Should not re-dispatch items that were recently audited and whose changes are non-semantic.
- **Producers:** A "Ready to close: Yes" item should stay ready unless changes actually affect the audit outcome.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automatic re-instatement detection:** When `isAuditNotReadyFresh` returns `false` (audit flagged as stale), the system automatically inspects the changes made since `auditedAt` and decides whether to re-instate the audit or flag for re-audit.
2. **Change inspection covers key fields:** The inspection examines description, comments, audit text, dependencies, and commit messages for changes that could affect the audit outcome. Non-semantic changes (e.g., metadata-only updates) do not trigger re-audit.
3. **Re-instatement logic:** If changes are deemed non-semantic (no impact on audit outcome), the original audit is re-instated by resetting `updatedAt` to `auditedAt` (same pattern as `saveAuditResult`). If changes are semantic, the audit is flagged as needing re-run.
4. **Full project test suite passes** with new regression tests covering re-instatement of non-semantic changes and re-audit flag for semantic changes.

## Constraints

- Change confined to audit freshness logic in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and the audit result management in the persistent store.
- No schema changes required.
- Must preserve existing audit behavior for items with no previous audit.
- Must be fully automatic — no operator intervention required.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:644`** — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`. If false, the audit is treated as stale.
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:1038`** — `saveAuditResult` resets `updatedAt = auditedAt` to keep audits fresh after audit writes.
- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`** — Audit results stored in SQLite; `getAllAuditResults` / `saveAuditResult` methods.

## Desired change

1. Create a new function `assessAuditInvalidate(changesSinceAudited, auditResult)` that inspects the delta between the audit time and current state.
2. The function should classify changes as semantic (affect audit outcome) or non-semantic (no impact).
3. For non-semantic changes, re-instate the audit (reset `updatedAt = auditedAt`).
4. For semantic changes, mark the audit as needing re-run.
5. Integrate into the `wl next` / TUI flow where audit freshness is checked.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` (line 644), audit map builder, sorting logic
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — Audit storage methods, `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line 747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` — Sync merge logic
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — Audit command integration point
- `src/pi-audit.ts` — Pi audit module

## Related work

- **WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO** — Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations (complementary; prevents timestamp churn, this handles post-invalidation review)
- **WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA** — Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn (child of WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO)
- **WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5** — Established the audit freshness rule (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Semantic boundary ambiguity:** What counts as a semantic change is subjective. **Assumption:** Changes to description, comments, dependencies, and commit messages are semantic; changes to assignee, tags, priority, and sortIndex are non-semantic. Document the rule in code comments.
- **Scope creep:** Requests for configurable invalidation policies. **Mitigation:** Keep this to the concrete scenarios identified; file separate items for broader policy changes.
- **Performance risk:** Inspecting changes since audit could add overhead. **Mitigation:** Only run when freshness check fails; use efficient diff comparison.
- **Backward compatibility:** Existing audit behavior must be preserved for items with no previous audit result.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What specific change types should the audit skill inspect when deciding whether to re-instate an audit? — A: Anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it. So description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages etc. Source: interactive reply (producer).
- Q: Should this be automatic (triggered when an invalidated audit is discovered) or manual (operator/producer-initiated)? — A: Automatic. Source: interactive reply (producer).
- Q: How does this relate to WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO (Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations)? — A: Complementary — WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO prevents timestamp churn from invalidating audits, this item handles post-invalidation review to determine whether to re-instate or re-run. Source: interactive reply (producer).

data.description:
## Summary

Make audit freshness **content-based** rather than write-time-based, by porting the
canonical content-fingerprint gate from the audit skill (SorraAgents,
SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) into ContextHub.

Today `isAuditFresh()` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) implements **only** the legacy
60 s time floor against `updatedAt`, so any metadata-only write (comment, sync merge,
lifecycle transition) marks a valid audit stale. A read-only review of the
`completed`/`in_review` queue found **22 of 52 items stale** and **12 with no audit at
all** (~65 % not fresh), almost none because the code actually changed.

## Problem

`updatedAt` is a *write* clock, not a *content* clock. It moves for reasons unrelated
to the audit's validity:

- `createComment` / `updateComment` / `deleteComment` unconditionally call
  `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`).
- sync merges re-timestamp items (95 items retimestamped to `2026-09-21T18:36:06` in a
  single sync; 244 items conflicted).
- `assignSortIndexValues()` (used by `wl migrate`) still bumps `updatedAt`.
- the audit runner's own verdict-driven status/stage transition happens *after* audit
  persistence and so stales the audit it just wrote.

The canonical algorithm is content-first, with the time gate only as a **legacy
fallback**:

> 1. fingerprint = HEAD sha + description hash + Key Files + working-tree state
>    (`git status --porcelain` + `git diff --name-only HEAD`); unchanged → fresh
> 2. time gate (floor): legacy reports use the 60 s gate

## Expected behaviour

- Each audit record carries a content fingerprint captured at persist time.
- `isAuditFresh` returns fresh when the stored fingerprint equals the current
  fingerprint, **regardless** of `updatedAt` movement caused by comments, sync merges
  or re-sorts.
- Audits without a fingerprint (legacy) fall back to the existing 60 s time gate.
- A genuine change to the auditable content (description/ACs, Key Files, HEAD,
  working-tree state) still invalidates the audit (stale).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `audit_results` gains a nullable `fingerprint` column via migration; existing rows
   are unaffected and remain readable.
2. `wl audit-set` (and the audit runner's `persist_audit.py` / `wl update --audit-text`
   path) records the fingerprint atomically with `audited_at`.
3. A single shared `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, storedFingerprint, currentFingerprint)`
   helper is the sole freshness definition; it returns fresh when the fingerprints match.
4. `updatedAt` churn alone (post-audit comment, sync merge re-timestamp, `sortIndex`
   re-sort) does **not** mark a fingerprinted audit stale.
5. A change to the description/ACs, Key Files, HEAD sha, or working-tree state marks
   the audit stale.
6. Legacy audits with no stored fingerprint fall back to the existing time gate
   (unchanged behaviour).
7. `stageDisplayIcon`, `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate`, and the
   ordering predicate all consume the same shared helper — no competing comparison.
8. Tests cover: comment-after-audit stays fresh; sync-bump stays fresh; description
   edit goes stale; HEAD change goes stale; legacy fallback.
9. Full test suite passes.

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- canonical algorithm: audit skill `SKILL.md` §Freshness Gate; SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT
- related-to: WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (P2 — sync-merge churn)
- evidence: `.worklog/logs/sync.log` (2026-09-21T18:35:58 → 18:36:17),
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` `isAuditFresh`, `packages/shared/src/database.ts`
  `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt`

## Summary

Stop `updatedAt` acting as a catch-all write clock for **comments**, so that a
post-audit comment (session log, dispatch note, audit note, close reason) can no
longer invalidate a valid audit.

## Problem

`createComment`, `updateComment` and `deleteComment` in
`packages/shared/src/database.ts` all call `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()`
unconditionally. The icon freshness predicate (`isAuditFresh`,
`AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS = 60000`) only tolerates comment bumps that
land inside 60 s of the audit. In practice comments arrive minutes or days later:

- `WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT`: audit `22:04:23`, `updatedAt 22:05:44` — 81 s, just past the
  window.
- `WL-0MTOBZZNU0009MW1` (+ 4 siblings): the `implement` "Start phase aborted" comment
  is the last write before the cluster that staled the audit.

The audit skill already documents this hazard and prescribes ordering (comment
**before** `wl audit-set`), but ordering is fragile and cannot protect against any
comment added later by another session or bot.

## Expected behaviour

- Comment activity is still recorded and visible (ordering, recency, FTS), but it does
  not move the audit-relevant timestamp.
- Semantic content edits (title, description, ACs, tags, parent, status, stage,
  priority, issue type, risk, effort) continue to bump the content timestamp.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A separate activity timestamp (e.g. `activityAt`) is introduced and bumped by
   comment create/update/delete; `updatedAt` is left untouched by comment writes.
2. Audit freshness is computed against the content timestamp, not the activity
   timestamp.
3. Ordering/recency features that currently rely on comment-updated `updatedAt`
   continue to work (or are explicitly re-pointed at `activityAt` with tests).
4. `WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT`-class case (audit then transition/comment > 60 s later) stays
   fresh.
5. Tests: add comment after audit → still fresh; delete comment → still fresh;
   description edit after audit → stale.
6. Full test suite passes.

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- related-to: WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9 (audit freshness after post-audit comments),
  WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R (flag-only flips must not invalidate audits)
- audit skill `SKILL.md` §Safety/prompt design — ordering contract SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM

# Ship-mode guard: block entry while project work is in progress, freeze on confirm

**Headline:** The herdr worklist gains a pre-dialog guard that refuses to open the Ship It confirmation dialog while any live agent pane (any workspace) is working on a work item belonging to the project, listing the blocking panes/work items; on `ship` confirmation it writes the Code Freeze marker immediately and clears it if the release command fails to dispatch.

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist lets an operator enter Ship It (dev→main release) mode even while other agent panes are actively working on the same project, risking a release of half-finished work. The worklist must refuse to open the Ship It confirmation dialog while any live agent pane in any workspace is working on a work item belonging to the project being shipped, tell the operator which panes/work items are blocking, and — once the operator confirms with `ship` — place the project into Code Freeze immediately (before the release command is dispatched).

## Users

- **Producers / release managers** using the herdr worklist who trigger dev→main releases.
- **Other agents** working on the project, who rely on the Code Freeze marker to refuse new implementation while a release is running.
- **User story:** "As a producer, when I press `S` to ship, I want the worklist to refuse and tell me which panes are still working so I do not ship over in-flight work. Once I have closed them and type `ship`, I want the freeze to apply at once so no agent starts new work mid-release."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Pressing the Ship It shortcut (`S`) when one or more **live** agent panes (machine-wide, across all herdr workspaces) carry a work-item ID belonging to the current project's worklog does **not** open the Ship It confirmation dialog. A notice is shown instead listing the offending work-item IDs (and pane labels where available) and stating that ship mode cannot be entered until the work is completed and those panes are closed.
- [ ] The blocking check runs **before** the confirmation dialog is rendered; the dialog is never shown while blocking panes exist.
- [ ] A pane only blocks when it hosts a **live** agent: a pane whose agent is absent, `done`, or `exited` does not block, even when its label carries a project work-item ID.
- [ ] When no blocking pane exists, pressing `S` opens the Ship It confirmation dialog exactly as today (no regression), and typing `ship` + Enter dispatches `/skill:ship release` as before.
- [ ] On typing `ship` + Enter (the confirm action), the worklist writes the Code Freeze marker at `<worklog-dir>/code-freeze.json` with `{ "active": true, "reason": "...", "startedAt": "<ISO>", "pid": <pid> }` **before** dispatching `/skill:ship release`.
- [ ] If dispatching `/skill:ship release` fails (no agent pane available, `onCommand` throws, or the dispatch is a no-op), the worklist **best-effort removes the Code Freeze marker it just wrote** and surfaces the error, so no stale freeze blocks the project once the release never started.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: the guard with blocking and non-blocking pane sets (live vs `done`/`exited` agents), multiple blocking panes, work-item IDs from a different project not blocking, the blocked-notice content, the pre-dialog gating (dialog not opened when blocked), the marker write on confirm, and the marker cleanup on dispatch failure.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and the Code Freeze marker contract docs.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Fail-open for browsing, fail-safe for the guard.** The existing Code Freeze reads are deliberately fail-open (a broken marker never blocks browsing). The new guard must fail *closed* only in the sense of not shipping on ambiguous pane data: an unreadable `herdr pane list` or `wl list` must not silently allow the ship dialog — surface the uncertainty rather than pretending the project is clear. (Decide and document the exact behaviour in implementation; recommendation: treat an unavailable pane/item query as "cannot verify — do not ship" and show the notice.)
- **No new dependency.** Reuse the existing primitives: `parseHerdrPaneListOutput` / `HerdrPaneRecord` (`downtime-worker.ts`), `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` (`hydrator.ts`), and the `code-freeze.ts` marker contract.
- **Project membership by work-item ID, not prefix.** Match pane-label IDs against the actual set of work-item IDs in the current project's worklog. A shared ID prefix across projects must not cause a false block.
- **Code Freeze marker ownership changes.** The marker is currently written/cleared by the ship skill and only read by the herdr plugin. This work extends the contract so the plugin writes the marker on Ship It confirmation; the ship skill remains the authority that clears it on release exit. Update the contract documentation accordingly.
- **No regression to the Ship It dialog.** The typed-confirmation behaviour (case-insensitive `ship`, Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel, bottom-anchored overlay) is unchanged.
- **ANSI rendering.** Any notice reuses the existing in-pane notice/dialog rendering helpers (`formatCodeFreezeDialog` pattern); no new dependencies.
- Follow build → test → commit discipline (vitest suite in `packages/herdr`).

## Existing state

- **Ship It shortcut / dialog** — `packages/herdr/src/ship-it-dialog.ts` (`ShipItDialogState`, `formatShipItDialog`, `overlayShipItDialog`) and `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`SHIP_IT_COMMAND = '/skill:ship release'`, `openShipItDialog()`, dialog key handling in `onData`). The dialog is opened from the chord-resolution branch when the resolved command equals `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`.
- **Code Freeze marker** — `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts` provides read-only helpers (`readCodeFreezeState`, `isCodeFreezeActive`, `readCodeFreezeStatus`, `readCodeFreezeStatusForRoot`) for `.worklog/code-freeze.json`; there is currently **no writer** in the plugin. The ship skill writes/clears the marker around the release.
- **Project ↔ pane matching** — `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` already lists in-progress items (`wl list --status in-progress`) and active panes (`herdr pane list`, machine-wide) and matches work-item IDs embedded in pane labels via `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`. `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` guarantees spawned pane titles preserve the work-item ID suffix, so labels reliably carry the ID.
- **Blocked-work UI precedent** — the Code Freeze notice (`code-freezeNotice` flag, `formatCodeFreezeDialog`, dismissal key handling in `worklist.ts`) is a full-pane modal used when an implement action is blocked.
- **Toast feedback** — `packages/herdr/src/notify.ts` (`showToast`) is fire-and-forget and may not be reliably seen; a blocking guard should use the in-pane modal notice pattern instead.

## Desired change

1. **New guard module** (e.g. `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts`): pure, injectable helpers to
   - collect the current project's work-item IDs from `wl list --json`;
   - list machine-wide panes from `herdr pane list` (reusing `parseHerdrPaneListOutput`);
   - return the **blocking** panes: panes whose label carries a project work-item ID and whose agent is live (agent present, status not `done`/`exited`);
   - format the blocked-notice text listing the offending work-item IDs / pane labels.
   Unit-test the pure logic with fixture panes (no real `wl`/`herdr`).
2. **Pre-dialog gate in `worklist.ts`**: when the resolved command is `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, run the guard *before* `openShipItDialog()`. If blocking panes exist, set a modal notice (listing the panes) and return without opening the dialog. The notice dismisses like the Code Freeze notice (Esc/Enter/q) and never dispatches.
3. **Immediate Code Freeze on confirm**: in `openShipItDialog`'s `onConfirm`, write `.worklog/code-freeze.json` (extend `code-freeze.ts` with a writer, e.g. `writeCodeFreezeMarker()` / `clearCodeFreezeMarker()`) before calling `executeResolvedCommand(SHIP_IT_COMMAND, ...)`. On dispatch failure / no-op, best-effort clear the marker it wrote and show the error.
4. **Tests**: a focused `ship-guard.test.ts` for the pure guard, plus TUI integration tests (in the style of `code-freeze-dialog.test.ts` / `ship-it-dialog-tui.test.ts`) that drive `S` with a real marker dir + injected pane resolver, covering blocked and clear paths and the confirm-time marker write/cleanup.
5. **Docs**: update `packages/herdr/README.md` (Ship It + Code Freeze sections) and the Code Freeze marker contract docs to record the new pre-dialog guard and the plugin-writes-on-confirm ownership change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts` — **new** guard module: project-item-ID set, blocking-pane filter, notice formatter (pure/injectable).
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.test.ts` — **new** unit tests for the guard.
- `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts` — add marker **writer/clearer** (currently read-only); document the plugin-writes-on-confirm contract extension.
- `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.test.ts` — tests for the new writer/clearer.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — pre-dialog gate in the `SHIP_IT_COMMAND` branch; modal blocked notice; marker write + cleanup in `openShipItDialog`'s confirm handler.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — reuse `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` (no change expected; reference).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reuse `parseHerdrPaneListOutput` / `HerdrPaneRecord` (no change expected; reference).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the guard and the marker-ownership change.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` / code-freeze contract docs — record the plugin-writes-on-confirm contract.

## Related work

- `Code Freeze: herdr plugin blocks implement actions (banner + dialog) during ship-it process (WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR)` — completed; the code-freeze banner/dialog and marker contract this guard extends.
- `Add Ship It shortcut with typed confirmation dialog in TUI selection screen (WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY)` — completed; the Ship It dialog whose `openShipItDialog()` is the gate point.
- `Code freeze should be in place from ship skill start, not just run-release.js execution (WL-0MT8MYGL3009QUZ6)` — completed; establishes that the freeze must start early, motivating the on-confirm write.
- `Downtime dispatcher must honour ship-it code freezes (no new implementations during freeze) (WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY)` — completed; the fail-closed consumer of the marker.
- `Implement: code-freeze detection, banner, implement-command blocking and dialog (herdr plugin) (WL-0MSBUCG73003MV3S)` — completed; the freeze infrastructure and dismissal patterns to reuse.
- `Herdr hydrator: rescue in_progress work items with no active pane (WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI)` — completed; the project ↔ pane matching primitives reused by the guard.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (producer, Q1 = a):** "work that is ongoing" means any live agent pane whose label carries a work-item ID from the current project — i.e. the rule is pane-presence, not item status. A completed item whose pane is still open still blocks; the operator must close it. Confirmed by the producer.
- **Assumption (producer, Q2 = list):** the blocked notice lists the offending work-item IDs (and pane labels where available) so the operator has an action list. Confirmed by the producer.
- **Assumption (producer, Q3 = cleanup):** on dispatch failure the plugin best-effort clears the freeze marker it wrote and surfaces the error. Confirmed by the producer.
- **Risk: ambiguous pane/item data.** If `herdr pane list` or `wl list` fails, the guard cannot verify. Recommendation: do not open the dialog and show the notice (fail-safe against shipping over unknown work); document the choice.
- **Risk: plugin-written marker left stale** if the plugin process dies between writing and dispatch, or the ship skill never clears it. Mitigation: clear on dispatch failure (Q3); document manual removal (`rm .worklog/code-freeze.json`) for the crash case.
- **Risk: performance.** Queries run on `S` keypress only; cache within the keypress to avoid a double `wl list`/`herdr pane list`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** blocking other actions (close/audit) during the pre-check, or scanning other projects' worklogs, is out of scope — record as separate work items if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

data.description:
# Ship guard always shows "Cannot verify pane state — cannot enter ship mode."

discovered-from:WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW — defect in the ship-mode guard feature (`packages/herdr`).
**Component:** `packages/herdr` — `createProductionShipGuardQuery` / `runShipGuard`.
**Severity:** High — the new ship gate is effectively always-on (permanently blocks ship mode) and shows a misleading reason.

## Symptom

Pressing `S` to open the Ship It dialog shows:

```
⚠ Cannot verify pane state — cannot enter ship mode.
Unable to check whether other panes are working on project items.
Please retry when the herdr CLI or worklog is available.
```

…even though `herdr pane list` works and open panes are actively working on the project. The notice lists no blocking panes (there is no action list for the operator).

## Root cause

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`createProductionShipGuardQuery`) runs `wl list --json` with `maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024` (8 MiB):

- `worklist.ts:3939` — `buildWlArgsForRoot(cwd, ['list', '--json'])` / `buildWlArgs(['list', '--json'])`
- `worklist.ts:3940-3943` — `exec('wl', wlArgs, { timeout: DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS, maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024 })`

The project's `wl list --json` output is **8,549,046 bytes** (2,298 work items) — **160,438 bytes over** the 8,388,608-byte limit. Node's `execFile` therefore rejects with:

```
ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER: stdout maxBuffer length exceeded
```

The `catch` around the `wl` call sets `worklogOutput = null` (`worklist.ts:3944-3946`). That makes `queryFailed === true` (`worklist.ts:5036`), so `runShipGuard` returns `ok: false` (`ship-guard.ts:216-222`) and the caller renders the generic `queryFailed` notice (`ship-guard.ts:167-172`).

The `herdr pane list` query succeeds (≈12,516 bytes) — only the **worklog** query overflows.

### Reproduction

```bash
cd /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub
wl list --json | wc -c        # 8549046
node -e "const {execFile}=require('child_process');const {promisify}=require('util');
promisify(execFile)('wl',['list','--json'],{encoding:'utf8',maxBuffer:8*1024*1024})
 .then(()=>console.log('ok')).catch(e=>console.log('THREW',e.code))"
# -> THREW ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER
```

## Why the message is misleading

- The notice says it "cannot check whether other panes are working on project items", but the pane query is fine; the failing query is the **project work-item ID set**.
- Because the worklog parse never happens, `blockingPanes` is empty, so the operator gets **no list of the offending panes/work-items** — defeating the "list the offending panes so the operator can close them" acceptance criterion (WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW) in this failure mode.
- It will not self-heal: the worklog only grows, so `wl list --json` will keep exceeding 8 MiB.

## Notes / contributing design

The guard needs the **full** set of project item IDs (a pane carrying a completed item still blocks — producer-confirmed semantics), so it loads the entire worklog. Building an ID set from an unbounded ~8.5 MB (growing) payload with a fixed 8 MiB `maxBuffer` is fragile. Possible directions (to be decided in implementation): raise the `maxBuffer`; add a `wl` IDs-only/bounded query; stream `wl list`; or match panes by a targeted per-ID lookup instead of loading all IDs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `createProductionShipGuardQuery` no longer fails when `wl list --json` output exceeds 8 MiB (clear-path guard still evaluates panes).
- [ ] A regression test covers a `wl list --json` payload larger than the previous `maxBuffer` (e.g. injected large output), proving the guard parses it and evaluates blocking panes.
- [ ] When the worklog query genuinely fails, the blocked notice distinguishes "worklog unavailable" from "pane list unavailable" so the operator knows which query failed.
- [ ] Full `packages/herdr` vitest suite passes.
- [ ] Documentation/comments reflecting the fix are updated.
